meta.description: Designs and validates quantitative targeted metabolomics assays (MRM/SRM on triple-quadrupole, PRM on high-resolution instruments) to report absolute concentrations. Covers the internal-standard strategy (external cal -> global IS -> standard addition -> stable-isotope-labeled IS), weighted calibration judged by back-calculated %RE not R-squared, ion-ratio quantifier/qualifier confirmation, matrix-effect/recovery characterization, and ICH M10 method validation. Use when quantifying a closed panel of known metabolites with units, building or validating an LC-MS/MS assay, choosing an IS or calibration weighting, or judging whether a reported concentration is trustworthy.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 8 cited references (MacLean 2010, Matuszewski 2003, ICH M10, Broadhurst 2018, Wang 2007, Teo 2020, Peterson 2012) are real, verifiable publications; no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics in any of the 5 executed/generated outputs, all of which derive numbers from computed synthetic data.

practice_boundaries.detail: Scope is bioanalytical assay validation and method development, not individual patient diagnosis or prescription; no diagnostic/prescriptive language appears in any output.

methodological_ground.detail: No output inverted a conclusion or committed a principled fallacy. Input 5 surfaced a real completeness gap -- SKILL.md's threshold table requires both intra- and inter-day precision acceptance but gives no formula for the correct nested-variance ('inter-day') computation, and a naive pooled-SD inter-day CV (18.9%) would have passed while the true intra-day CV (20.6-21.7%) fails -- but because the skill does explicitly require checking both tiers, the generated code checked both and reached the correct 'not fit for use' verdict. Recorded as a P1 recommendation, not a veto.

code_usability.detail: All R code across 5 inputs (calibration/back-calc, IS normalization, LOD/LLOQ, ion-ratio + matrix factor, full ICH M10 validation + carryover) ran to completion with base R + ggplot2 only, no missing dependencies, no syntax errors. The skill's own bundled example (examples/targeted_quantification.R) ran unmodified on first try.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of calibration/weighting, IS normalization, ion-ratio, LOD/LLOQ, decision-tree IS/validation strategy, and ICH M10 thresholds; runnable code exists for calibration/IS-normalization/ion-ratio but not for the promised full validation-metrics step (precision/accuracy per QC level, matrix factor, carryover, recovery) -- an agent must synthesize that code from a threshold table alone (confirmed in Input 5).

reliability.note: Hard-stop / NA-below-LLOQ is correct defensive design per the Category-3 scene override; boolean pass/id_confirmed flags are structured, agent-parseable signals rather than prose error messages. No documented handling for missing calibrator levels, non-monotonic curves, or negative back-calculated concentrations.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is a compact 211 lines with usage-guide.md carrying prompts/prerequisites separately; workflow is linear with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Learnability and consistency are strong (terminology and code patterns match across SKILL.md/usage-guide/example, verified by direct reuse in all 5 inputs); Error Prevention is excellent (Common Errors + Per-Method Failure Modes tables, verified accurate in Inputs 2/3/5); Feedback Design has a minor gap -- no explicit final-report/output-format template is specified.

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md's natural-language example prompts aid discoverability; the frontmatter description itself is technically dense (MRM/SRM/ion-ratio jargon), a minor risk for non-expert phrasings. Strict-input-rejection posture is intentional per the Category-3 Forgiveness override, not a defect.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw strings, no unsafe input handling; all code reads local numeric data only.

maintainability.note: Content is well modularized by concern (calibration, IS-normalization, ion-ratio, LOD, failure modes); the one bundled example script is deterministic (set.seed) and reproduced exactly in this audit. No scripts/ directory or bundled expected-output fixture beyond that one example.

agent_specific.note: Trigger description explicitly scopes itself against 3 sibling Skills (xcms-preprocessing, statistical-analysis, isotope-tracing) to prevent mis-triggering; strong escape-hatch culture (upfront 'three inputs the code cannot supply', single-transition method flagged as a documented compromise). Minor Progressive Disclosure deduction for keeping most code inline in SKILL.md rather than a scripts/ directory.

inputs.label: Full ICH M10 validation (intra/inter-day accuracy+precision, carryover) for a clinical PK assay
inputs.note: executed: true. Correctly flagged a planted intra-day LLOQ precision failure (CV 20.6-21.7% both days) and a planted carryover failure (427% of LLOQ vs 20% threshold); overall verdict correctly 'not fit for regulated PK decision'. Exposed a real SKILL.md gap: the threshold table requires intra- AND inter-day acceptance but gives no formula for computing inter-day precision correctly (nested variance vs. naive pooled SD) -- a naive pooled-SD inter-day CV (18.9%) alone would have passed the same failing LLOQ level (run/input5_stress_ich_m10.R).

assertions.text: Carryover correctly flagged as failing the <=20%-of-LLOQ threshold
assertions.note: Computed 427.2% of LLOQ from the planted high blank-after-ULOQ signal.

assertions.text: Intra-day LLOQ precision correctly flagged as failing (CV>20%)
assertions.note: Day 1 CV=21.7%, Day 2 CV=20.6%, both above the 20% LLOQ tolerance.

assertions.text: Overall assay verdict correctly concludes 'not fit for regulated PK decision'
assertions.note: all_acc_prec_pass=FALSE and carryover_pass=FALSE correctly combine to an overall FALSE verdict.

assertions.text: LOW/MID/HIGH QC tiers correctly pass accuracy and precision (clean planted data)
assertions.note: All 3 tiers within +-15% accuracy and <=15% CV, both intra- and inter-day.

key_strengths: Calibration/back-calculated-%RE code is directly executable and, verified against planted-truth synthetic data spanning 3 orders of magnitude, recovers concentrations within ~1% error (Input 1).

Extensive, citation-backed 'Common Errors' and 'Per-Method Failure Modes' tables (deuterium isotope effect, isotopic crosstalk, pre-analytical degradation) produced accurate, correctly-scoped advisory answers in Inputs 2 and 3.
Ion-ratio confirmation and IS-normalized matrix-factor code correctly distinguished one planted isobaric interference from six clean QC lots (Input 4).

Clear escape-hatch culture: explicitly names the three inputs code cannot supply (authentic standard, co-eluting SIL-IS, per-analyte validation record) and flags single-transition methods as 'a documented compromise, not a default.'

recommendations.title: No runnable code for accuracy/precision/matrix-factor/carryover validation metrics
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's 'What the Agent Will Do' step 6 promises computing accuracy, precision, matrix factor, recovery, and carryover, but only calibration/IS-normalization/ion-ratio ship as code; the Quantitative Thresholds table states both intra- and inter-day precision must pass but gives no formula for the correct inter-day computation.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill documents ICH M10 acceptance thresholds as a reference table rather than as runnable code, unlike the calibration and ion-ratio sections which pair the threshold with a code block.
recommendations.fix: Add a code block for precision/accuracy-by-level-and-day (explicitly using a nested/ANOVA variance-components model for inter-day, not a pooled SD across days), matrix-factor-across-lots, and carryover, matching the style of the existing calibration/IS-normalization/ion-ratio snippets.

recommendations.title: No explicit final-output/report-format template
recommendations.problem: 'What the Agent Will Do' lists 6 workflow steps but never specifies the expected shape of the final deliverable (e.g. a concentrations table with sample/analyte/conc/unit/flag columns).
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md focuses on methodological correctness (weighting, IS strategy, thresholds) and leaves output formatting to agent discretion.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Report Format' example showing the expected final table/columns, mirroring the calibration code block's style.

recommendations.title: Description is jargon-dense for non-expert trigger phrasing
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description relies on MRM/SRM/ion-ratio/%RE vocabulary; a user phrasing a request without this vocabulary (e.g. 'how much of X is in my sample') may under-trigger relative to the untargeted-discovery sibling skill.
recommendations.root_cause: Description is written for an expert audience already familiar with targeted-vs-untargeted terminology.
recommendations.fix: Add one plain-language trigger phrase to the description (e.g. 'give me a concentration in units for a known compound') alongside the technical terms.
